Compute covariate balance before and after matching

Source: R/Balance.R
computeCovariateBalance.Rd

Computes the standardised mean difference (SMD) for each covariate before matching (the full study population from [createStudyPopulation()]) and after matching (the matched population from [matchOnTcps()]).

Usage

computeCovariateBalance(population, pnuData, balanceArgs)

Arguments

population

A data frame from [matchOnTcps()] containing at minimum `row_id`, `treatment`, and `stratumId`.

pnuData

A [PnuData] object providing `studyPopulation`, `covariates`, and `covariateRef` tables.

balanceArgs

A `BalanceArgs` object from [createBalanceArgs()].

Value

A tibble with one row per covariate and columns:

`covariateId`

Numeric covariate identifier.

`covariateName`

Human-readable name from `covariateRef`.

`beforeMatchingMeanTarget`

Weighted mean in switchers before matching.

`beforeMatchingMeanComparator`

Weighted mean in comparators before matching.

`beforeMatchingSmd`

SMD before matching.

`afterMatchingMeanTarget`

Weighted mean in switchers after matching.

`afterMatchingMeanComparator`

Weighted mean in comparators after matching.

`afterMatchingSmd`

SMD after matching.

Rows are sorted by descending `|beforeMatchingSmd|`.

Details

**Before matching** uses uniform per-arm weights (simple unweighted means).

**After matching** uses stratum-size weights: each person in a matched set of size \(n_s\) receives weight \(1/n_s\), then weights are normalised to sum to 1 within each arm. This mirrors CohortMethod's approach and gives equal influence to each matched set, regardless of the number of comparators matched per switcher.

The SMD formula is $$SMD = \frac{\bar{x}_1 - \bar{x}_0}{\sqrt{(\hat{p}_1(1-\hat{p}_1) + \hat{p}_0(1-\hat{p}_0))/2}}$$ using the Bernoulli pooled variance of the group means.

The "before" population is read from `pnuData$studyPopulation`, which is populated by [createStudyPopulation()] and is not modified by [matchOnTcps()].

References

Suissa S, Moodie EE, Dell'Aniello S. Prevalent new-user cohort designs for comparative drug effect studies by time-conditional propensity scores. *Pharmacoepidemiol Drug Saf* 2017;26(4):459-468. doi:10.1002/pds.4117

See also

[createBalanceArgs()], [matchOnTcps()], [createStudyPopulation()]

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
simArgs <- createSimulationArgs(
  nSwitchers = 500L, nCovariates = 5L,
  prevalenceDiff = 0.3, seed = 1L
)
pnuData <- simulatePnuData(simArgs)
pnuData <- createStudyPopulation(pnuData, createStudyPopulationArgs(outcomeId = 1L))
pop <- dplyr::collect(pnuData$studyPopulation)
pop <- fitTcps(
  pop, pnuData,
  createTcpsArgs(
    prior = Cyclops::createPrior("normal", variance = 0.1),
    control = Cyclops::createControl(noiseLevel = "silent")
  )
)
matched <- matchOnTcps(pop, createMatchingArgs())
balance <- computeCovariateBalance(matched, pnuData, createBalanceArgs())
Andromeda::close(pnuData)
} # }
